stages.title: Sources
stages.what: The thesis corpus has nine sources. Tier 1 is Caltech CS 156: the book scan, its e-chapters, 18 slide decks, 8 homeworks, the final and the 18 lecture videos. Eight textbooks join it: ISLR2, ESL, PRML, MLAPP, Goodfellow's Deep Learning, UML, Mohri's Foundations of ML and Mitchell's Machine Learning, with the solution PDFs we have. Two libraries go through the same steps on their own track: the Zotero paper library and 37 learning books.
stages.why: The thesis asks about one course. CS 156 was chosen for fit, not popularity: in our adoption pilot only 1 of 43 universities lists its book. The textbooks are the ones the course maps to chapter by chapter; they give the graph more than two lecture voices.
stages.rejected: Taking the most-adopted books as Tier 1 (they fit the course less well).
numbers: Zotero papers with a PDF (latest snapshot)
stages.lost: Rights are not cleared by use: the books, slides and keys are "all rights reserved". Their text stays in private folders; the site shows ids, counts and short quotes only.
src: Thesis - Corpus and Question Bank Process §1

stages.title: Where compute runs
stages.what: The Mac only orchestrates: it plans work units, cuts pages out of PDFs, uploads, checks and merges. Every heavy step runs on a remote machine: OCR, embedding and the entailment checkers on free GPUs (Kaggle, Colab, the university's A100 slice), GROBID on Kaggle CPUs. A small SQLite ledger records every unit, so a finished unit is never leased again and a failed one can be retried. Private text goes only to private datasets and kernels, which are deleted after download and checked absent by listing.
stages.why: The Mac has 8 GB of memory. OCR on it did 3 pages in 10 minutes before it was stopped; embedding ran at 0.25 chunks per second under swap. Free remote GPUs did the textbook OCR in under two hours of wall clock.
stages.rejected: OCR, embedding or model inference on the Mac (too slow, swap).
numbers: Textbook OCR: kernels / wall clock / summed OCR-call time
170.3 T4-hours, 65 GPU kernels, about 8.7 h wall clock
Colab T4, about 3 GPU minutes for 5,639 new texts
Vector agreement, university GPU vs Kaggle
stages.lost: Free quotas run out and machines drop jobs: several kernels vanished mid-run and were re-run from the ledger. Dataset privacy is read back; complete remote erasure is checked by listing, not proven.

stages.title: Route by text layer
stages.what: Each file, and for the learning books each page, is sorted by one question: is the text layer usable for what we need? A scan or a maths-heavy page goes to OCR. A clean text page is read from its text layer. Papers go to GROBID (structure and references from the text layer) and only maths-heavy or scanned papers to OCR. Captions come straight from YouTube.
stages.why: OCR costs about 16-22 seconds of GPU time per page. A clean text layer is cheaper, and a garbage one (one copy of the e-chapters is a phone scan with a broken layer) must not get in. All thesis textbooks went to OCR because every one is maths-heavy.
stages.rejected: One tool for every file (wastes GPU time, or misses scans).
numbers: Learning books, per page: MinerU / text layer
8,858 / 4,613 of 13,471 pages (about a third of the GPU pages saved)
text layer of the official PDFs (100 items mapped)
stages.lost: The page router decides from cheap signals (text-layer words, formula density); a page it sends to the text layer keeps the text layer's errors.
src: OCR and Document Parsing Models - Research Note

stages.title: OCR with MinerU2.5-Pro
stages.what: Pages are rendered at 200 dpi on the remote worker and read by MinerU2.5-Pro, a 1.2-billion-parameter vision-language model. It writes Markdown with LaTeX maths, keeps printed page numbers and problem numbers in the pages we checked, and crops figures. Figure crops of the papers get their own text OCR, as a search aid.
stages.why: The first run (docling with EasyOCR) garbled inline maths and dropped words next to maths. In a 14-page pilot MinerU2.5-Pro was preferred on our own pages (LaTeX, page and problem numbers, figure crops); it has Apache-2.0 weights and fits a free T4 GPU.
stages.rejected: docling + EasyOCR (garbled inline maths); DeepSeek-OCR 2 (slower, 13.9 GB, dropped page numbers); PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 (environment failure, not a quality verdict); LightOnOCR-2 (timeout); Mistral OCR (paid, text leaves the machine).
numbers: Textbook pages: units done / failure markers
5,694; 290 of 290 units on the first attempt / 0
Textbook prose agreement with the PDF text layer (median per book)
stages.lost: Formulas are not checked beyond brace balance; a 15-page LLM audit of the course OCR found 47 notation-style losses in 278 maths spans (\mathcal, bold) and no corpus-wide error bound exists. Model-written figure descriptions can invent content, so they are flagged and kept out of the embedded text.
src: Thesis - Corpus and Question Bank Process §4-6

stages.title: Markdown with page markers
stages.what: Each source becomes one Markdown file with headings, LaTeX, figure links and page markers that carry the PDF page and the printed page. Papers become one Markdown file each plus a citation list. Captions keep timestamps; questions become rows.
stages.why: Markdown makes the structure explicit: headings (future sections), page markers (future citations) and tables. The choice is inferred: no controlled study compares Markdown with plain text for graph extraction.
stages.rejected: .txt (flattens structure); markitdown as a corpus converter (text-layer only, no layout or maths).
numbers: Book scan file: headings / x.y sections / x.y.z sections
stages.lost: Headings come from the OCR, so some are wrong (a sentence fragment can become a heading). The next stage checks them against the book's own outline.
src: OCR and Document Parsing Models - Research Note (Answer 2)

stages.title: Table-of-contents structure
stages.what: Each book gets a tree: book, chapter, section, subsection, each with PDF and printed page ranges. The PDF outline is cross-checked against a MinerU heading on the same page; books without an outline take their chapters from the OCR chapter openings. Every page and heading is tagged with its chapter and section.
stages.why: A page is a cut of the printer, not of the topic. A section keeps one topic, gives the graph its provenance, and gives the citation book, chapter, section and printed page.
stages.rejected: Page-bound units.
numbers: Books without a PDF outline (structure from OCR headings)
Headings of an outline node not found on its start page
48 (the unit then starts at the page start)
stages.lost: Outlines can be coarse (UML's has no chapter numbers) and one book's printed-page offset is not constant; printed pages are interpolated only when both neighbours agree.

stages.title: Lecture transcripts
stages.what: The uploaded English caption tracks are downloaded with yt-dlp and grouped into timestamped paragraphs: a new paragraph starts at a sentence end after 40 seconds, or after a gap above 6 seconds.
stages.why: All 18 lectures have uploaded (not automatic) captions, so no speech recognition was needed.
stages.rejected: Whisper, automatic captions (not needed).
stages.lost: Captions are not proofread: spoken formulas and names can be wrong.
src: Thesis - Corpus and Question Bank Process §3

stages.title: Question bank
stages.what: Questions that already exist (homework, final, book exercises) are parsed into one row per item, with id, page, LaTeX text, answer source and answer status. Book exercises are found by rules, one label pattern per book, with no language model. Exercises and solutions live in their own tables and never enter the retrieval units.
stages.why: A question set that we wrote ourselves is hard to defend. Existing questions with official keys are the strongest gold we have, and keeping solutions out of the passages stops the retriever from finding the answer key.
stages.rejected: Writing our own questions as the main set; leaving exercises inside the book units.
numbers: Course items / with an official key
Book exercises (rule-based) / with an answer source
Experiment bank: CS 156 + PRML official solutions
Reference answers outside the official keys: Opus drafts, Codex checks (agree / agree-skip / partial / disagree)

Strata by two blind taggers (Codex, Claude): exact / primary-membership agreement
stages.lost: Official keys are used as they are; every other reference answer is verified by two model families, and each item records who provided its answer. The primary stratum Q_prim holds only the items that both taggers put in PREREQ or CROSS; with κ 0.20 on membership, the taggers often disagree.

stages.title: Cleaning and units
stages.what: Rules clean the Markdown (running headers, page-number lines, footnotes, hyphenation, spacing) and keep the page markers. Then each table-of-contents node's own text becomes one unit, so no text repeats across levels. A unit above 1,024 bge-m3 tokens becomes a parent with children cut at paragraph, then sentence boundaries. Figure descriptions become their own figure rows.
stages.why: One citation per unit, and every unit fits the embedder's window. Rules only, no language model, so the cut is deterministic and every unit id can be recomputed.
stages.rejected: A fixed-size chunker that ignores sections; an LLM cleaner (not reproducible).
numbers: Figure rows (with image file, page and box)
Rows taken out of retrieval (figure-only or empty after cleaning)
stages.lost: The text-layer agreement check ignores maths, so a low value flags a page to look at, not an error rate; 252 pages are on a review list.

stages.title: Embedding with bge-m3
stages.what: Each unit becomes a 1,024-number dense vector and a sparse word-weight vector with BAAI bge-m3 (fp16, pinned revision), on a remote GPU. The embedded text leaves out model-written figure descriptions and every page-marker comment; the stored text keeps them.
stages.why: Over the transcript chunks, bge-m3 had the highest observed recall@10 of four arms from three models; its lead over Qwen3 was not statistically resolved. It also has Persian evidence.
stages.rejected: EmbeddingGemma 2 (12 points lower; our rule needed +10 to switch); Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (no resolved difference, stays the challenger).
numbers: Thesis corpus: dense rows / figure rows
Recall@10 smoke test, any required passage (not a result: run before the gold was locked)
Zotero library: unique vectors (body / references / figures)
stages.lost: A unit of 1,023-1,024 content tokens loses up to 2 tokens to the model's special tokens (flagged).
src: Thesis - Corpus Cleaning and Units (Embeddings v2)

stages.title: Postgres + pgvector, BM25, RRF
stages.what: In the tutor app the units and vectors live in PostgreSQL with pgvector; a BM25 index sits beside it; the two ranked lists are joined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 60) and reranked by a cross-encoder. The thesis arms read a pinned, hashed snapshot of the same passages with one fully specified BM25. The text arm R was tuned on the development split: 30 passages from each list, then the cross-encoder reorders the top 10.
stages.why: Vectors miss exact rare words ("KKT"); keywords miss paraphrases. Postgres's own ranking (ts_rank) does not use corpus-wide statistics, so it is not BM25.
stages.rejected: Postgres ts_rank as BM25; a graph store inside Postgres (Neo4j instead).
numbers: Thesis R, chosen on the dev split: depth / rerank_top
same stack on live tables; the thesis reads the hashed snapshot
stages.lost: The hybrid's gain over BM25 alone is not measured. With two lists, RRF can let one list dominate the fused top (a threats line in the thesis).

stages.title: Cross-encoder scores
stages.what: A cross-encoder (bge-reranker-v2-m3, int8 ONNX, on CPU) scores every question-passage pair the arms can need, once, before tuning. R reorders its top 10 with these scores, and the graph rank uses them inside each hop. All scores come from one scorer source, S1: it was kept because a 200-key overlap check was bit-equal on every kernel, on two CPU types.
stages.why: One scorer, set before tuning, so no result depends on which machine scored a pair. int8 scores differ across processor types (a Mac check gave 0 of 50 bit-equal), so the check had to pass on the machines that did the work.
stages.rejected: Scoring at question time per arm; mixing int8 CPU scores with an fp32 GPU re-score (the fallback S2 was not needed and did not run).
stages.lost: Every pair is cut at 512 tokens, the same cap for every arm; it may weaken the ordering for long exercise stems (a threats line, effect not measured). Full story: the page "One scorer, set before tuning".

stages.title: Extraction of typed edges
stages.what: An LLM reads each unit and writes edges from a closed list of three relations: PREREQUISITE_OF (learn this first), IS_A and USES. Every edge must quote its unit word for word; code drops edges whose quote or endpoints do not check. For the thesis graph the extractor is Claude Opus 5.5 with one fixed prompt, 25 units per batch.
stages.why: A closed relation list keeps the graph comparable and testable; the verbatim quote ties every edge to a passage. We tried to replace the large model with a small open one (Qwen3-4B, distilled from its labels): it lost 0.18 F1 on IS_A and 0.08 on USES against held-out references, so the large model stays.
stages.rejected: Open relation names; the distilled 4B student (measured worse than its teacher).
numbers: Edges kept by the rule checks
stages.lost: The extractor agrees with itself only partly (test-retest F1 0.64 in the distillation experiment): the graph is sparse, not complete. Course text goes to the LLM provider.

stages.title: Entity resolution
stages.what: Names that mean one thing become one concept: a normaliser, seed aliases, fuzzy matching, then bge-m3 name vectors; an LLM judge reads the passages of each uncertain pair. A model from another family audits a sample. Every merge is logged.
stages.why: "SVM" and "support vector machines" must be one node, or the graph splits one idea in two; "hard margin" and "soft margin" must stay apart. A merge after the freeze would change the snapshot hash, so all merges come first.
stages.rejected: A judge that decided from names alone (its reasons were copied; rejected); freezing before the 0.80-0.88 similarity band was judged.
numbers: Name groups / concepts after the first pass
stages.lost: The judge and the audit are LLMs.
src: Entity Resolution and Canonicalization - Research Note

stages.title: Entailment gate
stages.what: Two small checkers (HHEM and MiniCheck) score whether the whole unit supports each IS_A and USES edge. An edge is supported when both say so. PREREQUISITE_OF edges skip the checkers: the prerequisite judge (next stage) decides them.
stages.why: An LLM can write an edge that its own quote does not support. Cutting long passages at 512 tokens made the checker much worse in an earlier test, so the whole unit is the premise.
stages.rejected: Trusting the extractor's edges without a check; truncated premises.
numbers: Pair level, before the final merges: pairs / both support / both reject / disagree
Assertion level (the thesis figure): supported / disagree / rejected
Long-premise test (76 pairs): MiniCheck, whole vs 512-token cuts
stages.lost: The threshold 0.5 is the checkers' own boundary, not calibrated on our text.

stages.title: Prerequisite judge and restore
stages.what: Claude Opus 5.5 judged every PREREQUISITE_OF candidate with its evidence quotes and passage: keep or drop, with an error type. Its first rubric asked whether the source is needed to understand the target, and it dropped teaching-order prerequisites (a problem before its remedy, a base method before its extension). Rubric v2 counts teaching order: two blind re-judges (Codex and fresh Opus instances) re-read the drops, and an edge comes back only when both keep it. Load rule (policy 3): an edge is loaded when the extractor asserted it and either both checkers support it, or it is PREREQUISITE_OF and the judge kept it or both re-judges restored it.
stages.why: A blind audit found 11 of 50 loaded prerequisite edges wrong, mostly a motivation or a limitation read as a prerequisite, and no existing field could filter them.
stages.rejected: Loading every extracted prerequisite edge; rubric v1 alone (it dropped teaching-order prerequisites such as overfitting → early stopping).
numbers: Drops re-judged with rubric v2: restored / contested (kept out) / still dropped
Eligible PREREQUISITE_OF in the final graph
Blind audit of eligible prerequisite edges: before the judge / final graph
Final audit under the strict "necessary to understand" reading
stages.lost: The judge, the re-judges and the audits are LLMs. Codex was one of the two restore judges, so its final audit does not check the restored edges independently.
src: Thesis - Full KG Build (PRE judge, restore)

stages.title: Snapshot and freeze
stages.what: Concepts, assertions (with origin, gate verdict and review status), evidence, passages and merges are written as plain files, with a hash per file and one snapshot hash, S_G, in a manifest. The collapsed copy for arm Hc is made from the same files. Gold triples and test questions are written only after S_G.
stages.why: A text master copy can be diffed, reviewed and rolled back, and every experiment names the exact graph it used.
stages.rejected: The graph database as the only copy (hard to review and to reproduce).
stages.lost: Rule violations and judge drops are quarantined from the loaded graph, not deleted; the arms read only the eligible edges.
src: Building the Knowledge Graph - Pilot Slice

stages.title: Neo4j graph database
stages.what: The frozen snapshot is loaded into Neo4j, which serves the tutor app: typed walks at question time, the browser view and the graph view. Concepts link to passages by passage id, and the text stays in Postgres. The thesis arms do not query Neo4j: they read the hashed snapshot files. The load is checked by exporting it again and comparing hashes with the snapshot.
stages.why: The app needs bounded typed walks (two hops, chosen relations) while a student waits, and a graph database does them directly. An experiment needs a frozen artefact, which a live database is not.
stages.rejected: Postgres tables as the graph store; Apache AGE; SQL/PGQ.
numbers: loaded; all 5 exported files match the snapshot hashes
stages.lost: Neo4j's speed-up over a plain-file walk is not measured.

stages.title: Zotero paper library
stages.what: Every paper in the Zotero library becomes one Markdown file and a citation list: GROBID for papers with a usable text layer, MinerU for scans and maths-heavy pages, text OCR for figure crops; then section-aware chunks, bge-m3 vectors and Zotero tags. New papers go through the same stages with one command, which skips everything already done.
stages.why: Our own notes and the thesis cite these papers; a searchable library with page numbers lets every claim point at a page.
stages.rejected: Converting PDFs on the Mac one by one (markitdown); one tool for every paper.
stages.lost: No recall test against labelled questions yet; one encrypted or odd PDF can need a hand fix.

stages.title: Learning books
stages.what: 37 books for our own study (data, ML systems, software architecture, LLMs) go through the same steps: a per-page router, MinerU for the pages that need it, the same cleaning and units, and bge-m3. HTML and EPUB books are converted directly, with pseudo-pages.
stages.why: The same pipeline for every library means one query tool and one citation format.
stages.rejected: OCR on every page (about a third of the GPU pages were not needed).
stages.lost: Pseudo-pages of HTML and EPUB books cannot be cited by page; cite chapter and section.

EXP-002.title: Embedding pilot on CS 156: EmbeddingGemma-2 vs bge-m3 vs Qwen3-0.6B
EXP-002.result: EG2 768-d recall@10 0.35 vs bge-m3 0.47 (-12.0 points, paired bootstrap 95% CI -24.9 to -0.3). n=40, one LLM judge, transcripts only, dense retrieval only.
EXP-002.decision: Keep bge-m3 as primary embedder. EG2 256-d not recommended for storage. Re-test only on the 50-question set with book prose, Persian and BM25 fusion.

EXP-005.title: IUST vs Kaggle vector agreement (bge-m3)
EXP-005.result: All 350 chunks cosine >= 0.99998 (min 0.999989, mean 0.999999). IUST throughput about 20-21 chunks/s, peak 1.5 GB.
EXP-005.decision: Treat IUST and Kaggle bge-m3 vectors as interchangeable. Kaggle vs Colab not measured.

EXP-006.title: OCR model pilot: 4 models on 14 pages
EXP-006.result: MinerU2.5-Pro and DeepSeek-OCR-2 ran (MinerU best LaTeX, 3.3 GB). PaddleOCR-VL failed 3 times on the Kaggle image (CUDA library clash, PaddleX re-init; third attempt hung 3 h). LightOnOCR-2 returned nothing in 105 min on Colab. Read by eye, no error rate.
EXP-006.decision: MinerU2.5-Pro for the whole corpus (provisional). Do not re-run Paddle or LightOn on Kaggle; Paddle on IUST only with an isolated cu126 venv, and only if the benefit is worth it.

EXP-007.title: OCR production run: CS 156 course and solution pages
EXP-007.result: 104 units done on first attempt, 0 failed pages, 4 blank outputs; 20 s/page mean, peak 4.9 GB. 15-page spot check: 0 content errors in 278 math spans.
EXP-007.decision: OCR corpus accepted. Not re-run: dedup key (pdf sha1, page) per model, revision and dpi stops it.

EXP-009.title: Knowledge-graph pilot: NLI gate (HHEM + MiniCheck) on Kaggle CPU
EXP-009.result: HHEM 481 s, MiniCheck 1,518 s; 172 supported by both, 43 rejected by both, 104 disagree. First run lost MiniCheck (helper named minicheck.py shadowed the package); MiniCheck re-run alone. Off-ledger: hours = sum of the two stated model times, install and re-run not counted.
EXP-009.decision: Gate used in the pilot. Codex review: publish only as an auditable pilot demonstration.

EXP-010.title: Chunking strategies pilot: six arms over 18 lectures
EXP-010.result: Grade-2 share 23-30% across six arms; every paired-bootstrap interval vs our rule includes 0 (width up to 20 points). Inconclusive, not equal. Design confounds: sizes differ, 4,800-char cap truncates, overlap counted twice, no reference answers, correlated questions. 8 of 11 workers failed on adapter bugs (IUST lock HTTP 400, missing modules, Colab refusals).
EXP-010.decision: Do not cite as a finding. Do not re-run as designed; redo only with matched-size arms and token caps. Contextual retrieval and late chunking not run.

EXP-014.title: Long premises: HHEM + MiniCheck, whole vs chunked vs 512-truncated (76 pairs)
EXP-014.result: MiniCheck bal.acc whole 0.73, own chunking 0.61, splits 0.54-0.61; HHEM whole 0.58; 512 truncation 0.45-0.54. Split-evidence case (constructed): whole 17-18/20 vs splits 0-4/20. Labels by Claude. Bespoke-MiniCheck-7B run broken (all 0.0).
EXP-014.decision: Provisional: score whole premise up to MiniCheck's 2,048-token cap; never truncate at 512; HHEM as robustness score only; calibrate thresholds on human labels before reporting

EXP-015.title: Book corpus OCR: 8 books + 3 solution PDFs with MinerU2.5-Pro (parse to Markdown only)
EXP-015.result: 5,694 pages (8 books + 3 solution PDFs) OCR'd by MinerU2.5-Pro on 27 Kaggle T4 kernels (14 accounts, main not used) + 14 probe kernels; 290/290 units on attempt 1, 0 failure markers, 53 empty pages all blank in source; 28.93 h summed OCR-call time (18.3 s/page), 31.04 h worker lifetime + 1.18 h probes, 1.74 h wall clock; structure.json for 8 books; 1,327 exercises rule-extracted, 577 with an answer source
EXP-015.decision: Keep the Markdown, structure and question files as the book corpus. No new copyrighted shards to Kaggle (user books on IUST only); quality is metric-only, formulas need review on the listed pages

EXP-017.title: Corpus cleaning and units: rules-only clean, validate, units (8 books + cs156), hash-only manifest
EXP-017.result: 8 books processed (OCR complete), cs156 units rebuilt from existing text. update (units/2, no LLM): exercises and solutions moved out of the retrieval units into units/exercises.parquet and units/solutions.parquet (own rows, page + section + cut_from_unit_id, index=false); model-written figure descriptions kept, wrapped in generated markers, generated_by=ocr:MinerU2.5-Pro-2604-1.2B@d3f5e08; needs_human_review + review_reason flags; answer_provider/answer_status/ai_note/ai_proposed_answer/human_checked on the cs156 bank and the book items; see Notes/Thesis - Corpus Cleaning and Units
EXP-017.decision: Apply the user's decisions deterministically (no LLM): exercises and solutions in their own tables, generated text flagged, review flags, answer provenance.

EXP-018.title: Zotero full run: GROBID on 5,187 papers + MinerU2.5-Pro-fast on the routed ones
EXP-018.result: 5,186 of 5,187 papers in the library-text folder (3,076 GROBID route, 2,110 MinerU route); MinerU 29,835 pages, 0 failed, 170.3 T4-h unit time (tier A 99.6 h at 22.1 s/page, tier B 70.7 h at 19.2 s/page) on 15 accounts, 65 GPU kernels, about 8.7 h wall-clock; GROBID 128 units, 5,110 distinct PDFs, all HTTP 200, 3.0 CPU-h. 59,058 figure records (52,305 crops, 34,270 with text-layer words). Zotero tags: text: grobid 3,077, text: mineru 2,110, deferred-long 263. Lost compute: 2 GROBID CPU kernels and 1 GPU kernel (tp-35855501db, at most 0.3 T4-h) deleted remotely, all units re-run; 1 transient submit failure. Pending: JQA2GGB7 (encrypted PDF).
EXP-018.decision: Keep the mirror as the paper text layer for pdfmd and the Research RAG; defaults: Crossref off, threshold 0.4, long PDFs deferred.

EXP-022.title: bge-m3 re-embed of the thesis corpus after unit/text fixes (units/3, embed-hygiene/2): no empty rows, clean embedded text, whole figure rows with image and bbox
EXP-022.result: 8,515 indexable units (was 9,187): 655 figure-only + 14 comment-only children and 2 comment-only units set index=false, 1 child merged (only one merge fits the cap); old-new map in <slug>/units/unit_id_map.jsonl. 3,133 whole figure rows (was 3,724 pieces), 0 without image link, bbox or page. Embedded text has no comments or image syntax. Colab T4 only, worker tp-3c14a29cd7, commit 6de2fc9 clean (no +dirty), 5,639 new texts in about 3 GPU minutes, unchanged texts keep EXP-021 vectors; VM stopped, no Kaggle. Checks: norms 1.0, 0 NaN, ids and text hashes equal expected, 0 empty rows, pilot cosine min 0.9999974 (1,076 texts). Recall@10 smoke (proposed gold, 147 items): cs156 dense 0.59 / sparse 0.56 / RRF 0.60, all-books dense 0.48 / RRF 0.50: no change beyond noise. Codex astra: 11 findings, 10 fixed with tests, 1 documented (cap excludes 2 special tokens).
EXP-022.decision: Adopt v2 vectors (embeddings/bge-m3) as the current set; v1 kept as bge-m3.v1 and marked superseded. The fix is data quality, not a retrieval gain. 425 figures have no retrieval unit: the retriever must search the figure table too. Next: chunker design may reconsider the cap (1,022 content tokens) before any re-cut.
